prerequisites: It is recommended to have completed the core courses Manufacturing Engineering (2nd year) and Manufacturing Technology (3rd year)

learning_outcomes.text: Students should be able to gather and interpret relevant data (normally within their field of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
Students should have developed the learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.

Students should be able to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated by elaborating and defending arguments and solving problems within their field of study.
Applied knowledge of manufacturing systems and processes, metrology and quality control.
Ability to work, lead and manage conflicts in a multidisciplinary group and/or a multilingual environment.
Ability to apply new technologies including information and communication technologies.
Ability for information management, handling and application of technical specifications and necessary legislation for engineering practice.

syllabus_topics: Concurrent or simultaneous engineering
Design for assembly and manufacturing
Computer Integrated Manufacturing (CIM)
Simulation of manufacturing processes, computer-assisted
Rapid prototyping technologies
Parameter monitoring and manufacturing control, computer-assisted
Topic 1. Concurrent engineering.
Concepts on design for manufacturing: Product development stages, Product life cycle.
Concurrent Engineering.
Guidelines for implementing Concurrent Engineering.
Topic 2. Design for Manufacturing and Assembly DFMA.
DFM definitions and techniques.
Basic design criteria oriented to manufacturing.
Design guidelines for manufacturing. Injection Molding.
Design improvement to facilitate assembly: Types of assembly and design rules for assembly, Boothroyd-Dewhurst method.
Topic 3. Computer Integrated Manufacturing (CIM).
Digital manufacturing: CIM models, manufacturing aid software, industrial automation, main industrial control systems.
Manufacturing execution system.
Production planning.
Relationship between design, digital manufacturing, execution system and production planning.
Topic 4. Rapid prototyping technologies.
Introduction: Definitions, applications and types.
Additive manufacturing processes and technologies.
Stages of an additive rapid prototyping process.
Design for additive rapid prototyping.
Fused Deposition Modeling FDM systems based on extrusion.
Cost analysis.
Efficiency and sustainability in additive manufacturing.
Other applications and future of the technique.
Topic 5. Simulation of manufacturing processes.
Modeling and finite element analysis FEA.
Modeling of friction, fracture, contact and creep.
Modeling of plastic forming processes.
Modeling of the orthogonal cutting model.
Soft-computing techniques: evolutionary optimization, neural networks.
Topic 6. Parameter monitoring and computer-assisted manufacturing control.
Interest of process monitoring and control.
Measurement systems in conventional manufacturing processes.
Design of experiments.
Statistical process control.
Practice 1. Rapid prototyping. (Prepare digital files, configure FFF manufacturing, calibrate and prepare printer, and fabricate the part.)
Practice 2. Introduction to process simulation. (Make a simple numerical model with specific software for MEF simulation.)
Practice 3. Simulation of a plastic deformation process. (Make a numerical model to predict forces and deformations in a steel sheet under plastic forming.)
Practice 4. Measurement with electronic system. (Assemble and calibrate a measurement system with an electronic chain.)
Practice 5. Design of experiments. (Apply stages of experimental design to determine main factors of an experimental process.)
teaching_methods: Oral exposition with audiovisual aids for theoretical contents
Presentations and other consultation sources provided
Presentation of cases with photos/videos, examples, simulations

assessment_methods.method: Attendance and/or participation in face-to-face and/or virtual activities
Theoretical concepts exam or continuous assessment
Completion and presentation of assignments, cases or exercises (problem sets)
Attendance and submission of laboratory/field practices/ICT tool usage reports

assessment_rules: To pass the course, a minimum of 5 points (out of 10) must be obtained in the theoretical exam, and attendance at all proposed practical sessions is mandatory. The final grade will be calculated as: 0.1 * S1 + 0.5 * S2 + 0.2 * S3 + 0.2 * S4, where S1 is attendance/participation, S2 is the theoretical concepts exam, S3 is assignments/exercises, and S4 is laboratory practices.
